identification.summary: Earth Naga is Trend Micro's name for a China-aligned cyber espionage intrusion set that Trend describes as sharing compromised access with Earth Estries in what it calls a 'Premier Pass-as-a-Service' model [S1]. A Malpedia profile summarising the Trend report describes it as targeting government agencies, telecommunications and military-related manufacturers in the APAC region [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Search-result summaries of the Trend Micro report assess the Earth Estries and Earth Naga cooperation to date to at least late 2023 [S1]. First activity of Earth Naga itself is not established in sources opened.
identification.notes: Name is Trend Micro's (Earth- prefix). Search summaries of the Trend report equate Earth Naga with Flax Typhoon; other secondary profiles also list RedJuliett, Ethereal Panda and Storm-0919. These were not verified against the primary report or against Microsoft, Recorded Future or CrowdStrike, so no alias is added and the clusters are not merged [S1].

attribution.basis: Trend Micro characterises the activity as China-aligned [S1]. No sponsoring organisation or government attribution was found in sources reviewed.

objectives: Intelligence collection from government, telecommunications and related targets in the APAC region, per Trend Micro's description of the cooperation [S1].

targeting.notes: Trend Micro's report summary cites government, telecommunications and retail targets across APAC [S1]. Malpedia's claims of NATO-country and Latin America targeting could not be confirmed in re-check and were removed.

capabilities.summary: Malpedia's summary links Earth Naga to Draculoader and ShadowPad C&C infrastructure and to establishing SSH connections through compromised mail servers [S2]. Trend's central finding is that Earth Estries handed compromised assets to Earth Naga for continued exploitation, which complicates detection and attribution [S1].

campaigns.name: Earth Estries / Earth Naga access sharing (earliest assessed)
campaigns.summary: Trend assesses the access-sharing cooperation existed since at least late 2023, per search summaries of the report [S1].

campaigns.name: Joint operations against APAC targets
campaigns.summary: Trend's report summary describes the cooperation as observed against government, telecommunications and retail sectors across APAC [S1].

campaigns.name: Trend Micro publishes 'Premier Pass-as-a-Service' research
campaigns.summary: Trend describes Earth Estries acting as access broker for Earth Naga [S1]; Malpedia lists the report as dated 2025-10-22 [S2].

diamond.adversary: China-aligned intrusion set tracked by Trend Micro as Earth Naga, cooperating with Earth Estries [S1].
diamond.capability: Draculoader, ShadowPad, SSH tunnelling via compromised mail servers [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised mail servers used for SSH connections; ShadowPad and Draculoader C&C [S2]; access handed over from Earth Estries-compromised assets [S1].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing mail servers and other assets already compromised by a partner group [S1][S2].

gaps: WebFetch could not reach trendmicro.com or malpedia (DNS failure); the primary Trend Micro report 'The Rise of Collaborative Tactics Among China-aligned Cyber Espionage Campaigns' was not opened. Report details here come from search-result summaries and the Malpedia summary.

Alias equivalence with Flax Typhoon, RedJuliett, Ethereal Panda and Storm-0919 is asserted only in secondary summaries; Recorded Future's RedJuliett (Taiwan perimeter-device exploitation) reporting describes different TTPs and must not be merged until Trend's own mapping is read.
Sponsor, government attribution, confidence level, first-observed date and MITRE group ID are not established.
Specific CVEs, malware versions, IOCs and named victims were not obtained.
Secondary coverage (securityonline, hendryadrian, gurucul) was seen but without publication dates, so it is not cited as a source.
Fact-check: NATO-country and Latin America targeting, and the late-2023 and late-2024 to mid-2025 date ranges, could not be re-verified against opened sources; NATO/Latin America claims removed.
